why_this_target: customers are public entities, so the roster and their financial condition are both matters of public record

findings.finding: 23 of the 25 largest US counties and 21 of the 25 largest US cities are customers; 85% of the customer base is local government.
findings.why_it_matters: Establishes the overlap denominator. Vendor-sourced, because the company publishes its own client counts - marked as such.

findings.finding: At least 20 of the 25 most populous US cities reported budget gaps for fiscal year 2026.
findings.quote: at least 20 of the nation's 25 most populous cities have reported budget gaps
findings.why_it_matters: The other side of the overlap, from an independent research institution rather than the vendor.

findings.finding: Chicago, Los Angeles, San Francisco and Washington were all downgraded between December 2024 and April 2025; each of the three largest cities took a negative rating action in H1 2026, with New York City placed on negative outlook by Moody's and Fitch.
findings.quote: placing New York City on negative outlook
findings.why_it_matters: Named, dated stress at specific customers rather than a sector generalisation.

findings.finding: Only 45% of local government finance officers felt optimistic about meeting fiscal needs in FY2026, down from 64% a year earlier; the local government sector outlook is 'cautious' as expense pressure outweighs slowing revenue growth.
findings.quote: expense pressure is expected to outweigh positive but slowing revenue growth
findings.why_it_matters: A 19-point fall in finance-officer optimism in one year is the leading indicator for discretionary software budgets.

coverage.not_covered: roughly 14,975 other locations; all county customers
coverage.caveat: a budget gap is a pressure signal on a discretionary line, not evidence that any contract is at risk
coverage.vendor_sourced: the customer-count side is published by the company
